newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Gold demand rising as more in India marry.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Gold demand rising as more in India marry.

text.p: Rising personal wealth and more marriages are fuelling demand for gold in India, banking group Rothschild Australia Ltd said in a gold industry paper here.

India is the largest consumer of gold in Asia, mostly in the form of jewellery, said Rothschild Australia's managing director Richard Lee in the paper, scheduled to be delivered to a commodities conference here on Wednesday.
"There are an estimated 10 million wedding ceremonies each year, with an average of 30 grams (gold) bought for each wedding," Lee said.
Liberalisation of India's physical gold trading sector also has contributed to growth in demand for the precious metal, Lee said.

"The removal of restrictions on the issuing of gold lisences to goldsmiths has resulted in a flood of new producers on the market, contributing to a 82 percent increase in gold demand since 1991," Lee said.
India consumed 370.8 tonnes of gold in jewellery form in 1995, compared with 311 tonnes in the U.S., industry figures show, Lee said.
